papers.title: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a \$15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling

summary.tldr: StateM is an agent-native runtime that uses harness scaling—durable states, phase-local context, and versioned runbooks—to reach 95.3% raw accuracy on Terminal-Bench 2.1 without updating model weights.
key_points: Reaches 95.3% raw accuracy across 445 trials on Terminal-Bench 2.1 using GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh, achieving a 100% single-success rate across all 89 tasks.
Reduces API execution cost to $15 for the final run compared to $574.68 for the GPT reference run.
Improves open/alternative models, raising DeepSeek-V4 Flash from 82.7% to 88.1% under standard timeouts for under $38 in adaptation costs, and boosting GPT-5.6 Luna from 76.7% to 85.4%.
Organizes agent execution using durable states, recoverable runbooks, and stateful controls built from converted postmortem findings.
Demonstrates held-out generalization on BusinessBench, yielding gains of 0.55 macro and 1.34 micro points using family-specific runbooks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that runtime harness engineering can outperform model-scaling approaches for long-horizon agent tasks while drastically reducing API compute costs.

papers.title: Learn What's Left, Not What's Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization

summary.tldr: SA-MRPO replaces fixed scalarized rewards in multi-objective RL with independent per-objective standardization and dynamic saturation-based advantage reweighting.
key_points: Existing fixed weighted-sum methods waste gradient budget on saturated rewards and give identical advantages to rollouts with distinct reward profiles.
SA-MRPO standardizes each reward objective independently and dynamically discounts its advantage contribution based on batch-level objective saturation estimates.
Dynamic reweighting can invert the direction of policy updates rather than simply rescaling magnitude.
Empirically improves AIME24 accuracy by up to 5% over GDPO, adaptive reasoning accuracy by up to 9.2% on AMC23, and coding pass rates by up to 2.3% without degrading satisfied objectives.
summary.why_it_matters: It dynamically redirects model capacity toward unfulfilled objectives during post-training without requiring manual tuning of multi-reward weights or risking performance degradation on mastered tasks.

papers.title: Large Discovery Models: Empirically-grounded Model-Based Open-Ended Search

summary.tldr: The Large Discovery Model couples generative models with a Bayesian non-parametric reward surrogate and dynamic memory to enable uncertainty-aware, empirically grounded search across open-ended hypothesis spaces.
key_points: Pairs a generative model (like an LLM) for candidate generation and refinement with a Bayesian non-parametric surrogate that models reward and quantifies epistemic uncertainty.
Maintains a continually updated discovery memory and surrogate model that adapt immediately as new experimental observations arrive.
Achieves a 2.4x greater reduction in validation BPB for neural-network training compared to baseline search and reflection methods.
Demonstrates an 18.2% relative decrease in binding energy for antibody design and over 60% relative gains in multi-objective molecular optimization.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining generative priors with calibrated statistical surrogates allows AI systems to discover optimized molecules, proteins, and neural architectures far more reliably than LLM self-reflection alone.

papers.title: MOSS-VL Technical Report

summary.tldr: MOSS-VL is an 11.3B open vision-language model family co-designed for real-time interaction using gated cross-attention to process incoming visual frames while generating text.
key_points: Uses gated cross-attention to keep visual tokens outside the decoded sequence, expanding its time-to-first-token advantage over Qwen3-VL-8B from 2.8x to 5.1x as visual context expands.
Employs a staged curriculum that isolates real-time-specific training to a light final stage over an offline foundation.
Supervised by a synthesized interaction corpus to manage when to speak, remain silent, or revise output.
Outperforms open streaming baselines on three of four real-time benchmarks, achieving 66.0 vs. 37.5 on OmniMMI Proactive Alerting.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables open-source vision-language models to handle real-time proactive interaction and large visual contexts with significantly lower first-token latency.

papers.title: ASI-Bench: At the Dawn of Artificial Superintelligence

summary.tldr: ASI-Bench is a new benchmark featuring 60 project-level research tasks across 11 scientific domains to evaluate AI systems' autonomous exploration and execution capabilities as human methodological guidance is progressively removed.
key_points: Constructed by over 40 experts utilizing more than 31,000 human hours, with all tasks passing expert review, AI-assisted auditing, sandbox execution, and scorer validation.
Tests AI capability by systematically withdrawing methodological guidance across identical research projects to measure independence.

Evaluation of 18 state-of-the-art agent-model configurations showed average performance dropping from 50.91 under full guidance to 29.10 with specified methods, and down to 26.62 when agents independently select methods.
summary.why_it_matters: The dramatic performance drop under unguided conditions reveals that state-of-the-art AI agents remain heavily reliant on human guidance and are currently unable to autonomously execute end-to-end scientific research.

papers.title: FreeToken: Efficient Edge-Native MoE Serving with Bandwidth-Adaptive Execution

summary.tldr: FreeToken is an edge-native Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) serving system that dynamically adapts model layout, expert residency, and CPU-GPU execution to local, heterogeneous hardware resources.
key_points: Co-designs the serving stack around unified, elastic memory management, expert residency, CPU-GPU execution, and agentic state reuse.
Continuously maps computation and model state to fluctuating agent workloads and variable edge hardware balances instead of using fixed offloading.
Supports over 20 MoE models, enabling execution of a 35B model on an 8GB laptop GPU, a 284B model on a gaming desktop, and the 753B GLM-5.2 on a single workstation GPU.
Released open-source as deployable local software via flashml.ai.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables consumer-grade edge hardware and single workstations to locally serve frontier-scale MoE models that previously required datacenter infrastructure.

papers.title: Agentic ESOpt: Fine-Tuning Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Minimal GPU Requirements

summary.tldr: Agentic ESOpt is a full-parameter agentic fine-tuning framework using Evolution Strategies to train long-horizon LLM agents with minimal inference-level GPU memory requirements.
key_points: Replaces backpropagation-based RL with Evolution Strategies (ES) using online reward-weighted updates from sampled parameter perturbations.
Bypasses RL credit assignment problems by performing trajectory-level parameter attribution without reward decomposition across horizons.
Implements a cosine decay schedule for the perturbation scale \sigma to balance exploration and adaptation.
Supports online prompt-parameter co-evolution to combine parameter optimization with prompt-space evolution like test-time compute.
Full-parameter optimization of Qwen-3.5-27B yielded a 6.69% improvement over the No Skill baseline on WebArena-Lite.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables full-parameter fine-tuning of large LLM agents on long-horizon tasks using low-memory, inference-only hardware without the stability and compute overhead of multi-turn RL.

papers.title: How Do Agents Fail on AutoResearch: End-to-End Diagnostic Evaluation on 100 Real-World Frontier Research Tasks

summary.tldr: AutoResearchEval introduces 100 full-lifecycle frontier science tasks to diagnose AI agent failures, establishing a 45-pattern taxonomy based on 800 evaluated trajectories.
key_points: Evaluated 8 harness-model combinations across 100 tasks spanning 7 scientific domains and the entire research lifecycle.
Established the AutoResearch Failure Taxonomy (ARFT), categorizing 45 empirically-grounded failure patterns from intermediate artifacts and full trajectories.
Utilized a human-calibrated agent-as-a-judge pipeline for scalable, fine-grained trajectory attribution.
Identified a core model-level deficit across all configurations: the lack of a metacognitive loop to verify outputs, revise mistakes, and evaluate chosen research paths.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding systematically how autonomous research agents fail reveals that model-level metacognitive deficits, rather than scaffolding issues, currently limit end-to-end scientific discovery.

papers.title: Advancing Open and Reproducible Relational Learning: RelArena-α, TabPFN-Rel and RPI

summary.tldr: Prior Labs released an open-source alpha suite for relational learning comprising the RelArena-α benchmark framework, the TabPFN-Rel model harness, and the model-agnostic Relational Predictive Interface (RPI).
key_points: RelArena-α standardizes data loading, evaluation protocols, and tuning regimes based on RelBench v1 to enable reproducible method comparisons.
TabPFN-Rel adapts TabPFN-3 for relational databases, outperforming prior baselines by flattening relational databases into single-table representations.
RPI provides an open-source, model-agnostic interface allowing users to define prediction tasks on custom databases and run RelArena-α compatible models.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes standardized benchmarking for relational ML while offering tools to apply tabular models like TabPFN directly to relational databases.

papers.title: Embodied-Navigator: Point, Think, Memorize, and Align for Efficient Navigation

summary.tldr: TAMP-Nav is a unified embodied navigation framework that combines a 2D pixel-to-3D action formulation, dynamic selective reasoning with compressed memory, and GRPO-based two-level alignment.
key_points: Pixel-to-3D Action Formulation lets the VLM select 2D pixels that project to 3D coordinates for a low-level SLAM controller.
Selective Reasoning and Anchor-Trajectory Memory dynamically triggers Chain-of-Thought and compresses redundant trajectories into Space-Time Indicators at critical nodes.
Two-Level Alignment Paradigm uses Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to combine global outcome rewards with fine-grained process rewards.
Achieves 66.2% Success Rate (SR) on R2R-CE using 90k training trajectories.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves VLM deployment efficiency in robotics by aligning action spaces with 2D pre-training priors and reducing sample complexity.

papers.title: GRNEdit: Efficient General Video Editing from a New Binary-Evidence Perspective in Generative Refinement Networks

summary.tldr: GRNEdit is a lightweight two-stage video editing framework that models source video information as binary-evidence signals and refines target-bit decisions using a source-preserving identity pathway.
key_points: Recasts editing semantics into local retain-or-flip decisions over individual bits, modeling source features as coordinate-wise evidence.

Stage I uses a compact encoder (adding less than 3% conditioning parameters) to turn discrete source codes into continuous evidence signals and uses a null-prompt identity pathway for source reconstruction.
Stage II compares edited states against source-preserving counterparts from the identity pathway to calculate discrepancies and revise unresolved target-bit decisions.
Trained on 0.6M video pairs, GRNEdit-2B and GRNEdit-8B achieve scores of 4.03 and 4.18 on OpenVE-Bench, respectively.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that lightweight binary-evidence conditioning can outperform or match much larger 14B parameter video editing models while significantly reducing computational overhead.

papers.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: Towards Harnessed Agentic RL

summary.tldr: Agent Lightning v1.0 is a 3,500-line framework for harnessed agentic RL, enabling post-training of arbitrary agent harnesses through an LLM proxy.
key_points: Harnessed agentic RL shifts ownership of the environment interaction loop from the trainer to the harness, leaving the trainer to observe only LLM request-response pairs.
Addresses core challenges in retokenization, sample merging, advantage calculation, loss normalization, and backend scheduling.
Improves Qwen3.5-9B performance on SWE-bench Verified from 41.8% to 56.4% (+14.6 absolute gain) using 6K training examples.
Evaluated across instruction-following, search, and coding agents with fully reproducible scripts and workflows.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows developers to post-train language models directly within their existing production agent harnesses using minimal compute and data.

papers.title: CoinVE-200K: A Large-Scale High-Quality Dataset for Compositional Instruction-Guided Video Editing

summary.tldr: CoinVE-200K is a large-scale video editing dataset offering 1080p video pairs with up to 201 frames and 2 to 5 compositional editing operations per sample, paired with a benchmark and the 22B CoinVE-Edit model.
key_points: CoinVE-200K contains 1080p, up to 201-frame video pairs featuring 2 to 5 atomic editing operations spanning addition, removal, modification, and stylization across humans, objects, and backgrounds.
CoinVE-Edit is a 22B compositional video editing model constructed by combining Wan2.1-T2V-14B and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct.
CoinVE-Edit employs disentangled region-aware attention for distinct editing instructions to execute precise multi-region edits while retaining unedited content and temporal coherence.
The authors introduce CoinVE-Bench to evaluate compositional-instruction video editing across varied subjects, operation types, and instruction complexities.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides the dataset, benchmark, and architectural framework necessary to advance video editing models from single-intent tasks to complex, multi-operation compositional edits.

papers.title: TRACE-Bench: Decomposing and Diagnosing Multi-Reference Image Generation

summary.tldr: TRACE-Bench introduces a capability-oriented framework for multi-reference image generation, decomposing complex tasks into four atomic operators across 1,600 evaluation cases to precisely locate model failure modes.
key_points: Formalizes multi-reference image generation into four atomic operators: Anchor (f), Disentangle (g), Apply (oplus), and Compose (C).
Quantifies structural complexity by counting operator slots (spanning slot counts 1--8) across 631 formula templates and ~4,000 reference images.
Features an operator-aligned evaluation protocol and diagnostic tree analysis to recursively localize failures.
Benchmark evaluation of 9 leading models identified disentanglement (g) and attribute binding (oplus) as primary bottlenecks, with top model attribute fidelity peaking at 0.74.
summary.why_it_matters: By shifting from holistic task scores to granular, operator-level diagnostics, TRACE-Bench reveals that multi-reference generation failures stem from attribute binding and disentanglement rather than overall composition.

papers.title: Harness the Memory: A Holistic Evaluation of Memory Substrates in Memory Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers developed a unified controlled harness evaluation across 26 metrics to analyze how different memory substrates perform across various LLM backbones, history lengths, and task regimes.
key_points: Evaluated memory substrates including dense/sparse indices, text records, structural and hierarchical stores, refinement-based memories, parametric updates, and activation-compatible context mechanisms.
Tested performance across three LLM backbone models and four benchmark suites covering user-centric question answering and agent-centric sequential decision-making.
Measured 26 performance and efficiency metrics, finding that broad retrieval aids factual QA but harms sequential decision-making by distracting from action-critical context.
Demonstrated that substrate performance degrades or scales unpredictably at longer history horizons, highlighting the need for dynamic substrate routing.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings show that memory architecture must be dynamically routed based on task type and history length rather than relying on a single static substrate.

papers.title: Beyond the Trace: Coupling an Interpretable Reasoning-State Readout to Native MoE Routing

summary.tldr: Researchers developed J64, a 64-axis internal semantic readout for MoE reasoning models, and its routing-based proxy R64, enabling non-intrusive model monitoring, trace-free test-time intervention, and targeted router editing.
key_points: J64 distills vocabulary-scale J-space into a 64-axis semantic frame, separating inference effort from problem strain and adding 0.096-0.135 held-out AUC over token-occupancy baselines.
R64 reconstructs J64 using native MoE expert-routing statistics, achieving a median per-axis correlation of 0.69-0.86 with J64 and retaining 95-100% of its predictive gain on gpt-oss-20b.
R64-weighted voting outperforms standard majority voting in 7 of 8 completed candidate set settings.
During generation, a cumulative stop-and-resample policy driven by J64 improves accuracy by 1.1-5.9 points, with the R64 routing proxy capturing 0.9-3.2 of those points.
Direct edits to the router based on J64 diagnostics successfully shift model behavior from numerical guessing to exact symbolic execution during diagnosed stalls.
summary.why_it_matters: Native MoE routing statistics can act as a zero-overhead proxy for latent reasoning states, allowing real-time decoding interventions and targeted model edits without relying on generated token traces.

papers.title: MoNe: Modular Neural Memory for Efficient Long Context Inference

summary.tldr: MoNe is a lightweight modular neural memory that attaches to frozen Transformers, providing O(N) preprocessing and O(1) query costs for long-context inference without context re-reading or backbone retraining.
key_points: Attaches to frozen pretrained Transformers with a 6.4% parameter overhead and no full backbone retraining required.
Processes context in fixed-size segments using test-time learning of fast-weight neural memory networks via layer-localized gradient updates.
Generates keys and values strictly from query tokens during inference, decoupling query compute and peak GPU memory from context length N.
Reduces compute and peak GPU memory by ~80% at 128K context lengths compared to In-Context Learning (ICL).
Outperforms ICL on RULER needle-in-a-haystack and word extraction benchmarks when exceeding the backbone's native context window.
summary.why_it_matters: MoNe enables large language models to process extreme context lengths with constant-time query overhead and fixed peak GPU memory usage without fine-tuning the base model.

papers.title: Recirculation

summary.tldr: Recirculation is an inference-time architectural enhancement that introduces recurrence into feedforward transformers to track belief states without adding generation latency.
key_points: Introduces a recurrence mechanism to allow transformer feedforward layers to act as dynamical systems during inference, overcoming depth-bounded state updates.
Requires serial processing during the prefill phase but adds essentially zero latency during token generation.
Includes an adaptive variant that tunes hyperparameters while freezing original model weights, requiring no full model retraining.
Achieves a 23% perplexity reduction across dataset suites and a 21% accuracy increase on GSM8k when applied to the Gemma3 model family.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows foundation models to significantly improve generation and reasoning performance at inference time without requiring computationally expensive model retraining or adding token generation latency.

papers.title: Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF

summary.tldr: Reinforcement learning using a two-player adversarial debate game reduces reward hacking when an LLM policy is overseen by a weaker AI judge compared to standard RLAIF.
key_points: Evaluated on mathematics tasks by training a Gemini 2.5 Flash-class policy against a frozen, weaker Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite judge.
Debate training recovered 45% of the performance gap in peak validation accuracy over the RLAIF baseline, maintaining judge performance across extended RL steps.
Weakening the judge accelerated reward hacking, which was offset by adding an extra debate round.
Imposing a critique word limit (effective up to 150 words) prevented critic judge-hacking and balanced multi-agent RL dynamics at the expense of critic clarity.
RL with an LLM judge demonstrated a smaller train/validation reward gap compared to RL trained directly from verifiable ground-truth rewards.
summary.why_it_matters: Debate training provides a viable scalable oversight mechanism to prevent policy models from exploiting weaker AI evaluators as model capabilities advance.

papers.title: Chain-of-Experience for Continual LLM Improvement

summary.tldr: Chain-of-Experience (CoE) enables LLMs to continuously improve at test time by accumulating iterative experiential traces from self-feedback and environmental signals.
key_points: CoE evaluates 8 LLMs (including GPT-5, Gemini-2.5 Pro, and Claude-4.5 Sonnet) using self-feedback and environmental feedback across math, coding, and knowledge domains.
The method achieves a 5.6% overall accuracy improvement and 19% lower API costs compared to feedback-free baselines.
Combining complementary feedback channels yields additional performance gains while delivering higher accuracy per token than existing test-time strategies.
Models demonstrate robustness against weak or spurious feedback, with the majority of performance improvements emerging in early iterations.
summary.why_it_matters: CoE provides a token-efficient framework for continuous test-time model optimization without requiring retraining or manual fine-tuning.

papers.title: Decomposition Attacks Across Unlinkable Identities: Limits of Stateful Defenses for LLM Services

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that stateful defenses fail against LLM decomposition attacks executed across unlinkable identities, proving theoretical limits and achieving up to 100% attack success within two attempts across 10 tested defense policies.
key_points: Decomposition attacks bypass stateless LLM guards by splitting harmful tasks into individually permissible requests across unlinkable identities and combining answers offline.
Theoretical analysis proves that defense utility and security depend on benign request grouping; adaptive attacker retries using Allow/Block feedback eliminate valid defense operating points.
Empirical evaluation on 91 executable tasks and 11,393 capability-matched benign requests showed all 10 tested policies failed under strict false-positive budgets (1% matched, 0.5% background).
On defense-unseen task families, attack success reached at least 99% after one attempt and 100% after two attempts, even against a privileged policy with an exact request-to-operation map.
summary.why_it_matters: Stateful monitors alone cannot stop multi-identity decomposition attacks, necessitating structural mitigations like identity linkage, costs for fresh accounts, or restricted answer usage.

papers.title: PTXBench: Benchmark and Adapt LLMs for GPU Kernel Optimization with Architecture-specific PTX

summary.tldr: PTXBench evaluates and adapts LLMs for architecture-specific PTX GPU kernel optimization across GEMM and attention workloads on H100 and B200 GPUs.
key_points: PTXBench measures functional correctness, target instruction execution at runtime, and speedup over frontier libraries for GEMM and attention tasks on NVIDIA H100 and B200 GPUs.
Evaluated LLMs show significantly reduced success rates on complex attention backward workloads, and runtime instruction execution often fails to deliver competitive performance.
Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-27B with repair-conditioned training improves performance on several tasks, though generalization depends heavily on data balance, coverage, and teacher quality.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a standardized benchmark to measure and improve how well LLMs write hardware-specific assembly instructions to optimize deep learning kernels for new GPU architectures.

papers.title: What Tokens are Learned when Tokenization is Optimized Jointly with Language Modeling?

summary.tldr: Jointly optimizing tokenization with language modeling alters token structures, with SSLMs learning morphologically aligned tokens and H-Nets favoring byte-level efficiency over traditional subword vocabularies.
key_points: SSLMs recover morphologically aligned, contextually efficient tokens, while H-Nets prioritize byte-level efficiency by producing longer tokens with minimal subword vocabulary overlap.
Tokenization behavior adapts dynamically based on language structure, with agglutinative languages showing higher segmentation variability during training across 18 typologically diverse languages.
SSLM-based pretokenization in pretrained-then-finetuned BERT models consistently reduces language modeling perplexity and delivers competitive downstream performance despite using novel vocabularies.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that tokenizer-free, jointly optimized approaches effectively automate vocabulary creation by prioritizing contextual and computational efficiency over fixed morphological rules.

papers.title: Q-Interference: Memory-Efficient Phase-Aware Quantum-Inspired Attention

summary.tldr: Q-Interference introduces a memory-efficient, phase-aware quantum-inspired attention mechanism for GPT models using an exact trigonometric factorization.
key_points: Augments query and key features with an amplitude and a learned phase to enable constructive and destructive token feature interactions.
Addresses the high memory cost of naive phase-aware attention by deriving an exact trigonometric factorization that reduces computation to two standard matrix multiplications.
Avoids materializing a large token-pair-feature interaction tensor while computing the exact same attention score.
Integrates into standard Transformer blocks for autoregressive language modeling without modifying the rest of the model architecture or next-token prediction objective.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables richer, phase-aware feature interactions in Transformer attention mechanisms without increasing memory overhead or breaking compatibility with standard GPT pipelines.

papers.title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification

summary.tldr: A comprehensive re-evaluation reveals that memory-based self-improving agents suffer from extreme fragility due to amplified variance, sensitivity to task ordering, and task or environment underspecification.
key_points: Self-improving loops amplify evaluation noise inherent to complex, multi-step agent environments across multiple runs.
Agent performance improvements rely heavily on default task orderings, which implicitly act as a hidden curriculum prerequisite.
Task and environment underspecification contribute to memory failure modes.
Integrating detailed rubrics and environment feedback into memory construction partially mitigates performance degradation, but significant variance and performance gaps persist.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating self-improving agents requires multi-run protocols and randomized task orders to prevent false conclusions drawn from unstated curricula and environment noise.

security.title: COMA: A Compositional Misleading Attack Class on Security-RAG, and a Causal Counterfactual Defense

summary.tldr: COMA introduces a RAG attack where factually correct, benign documents compose to mislead security copilots, alongside a Causal Counterfactual Defense (CCD) that isolates adversarial influence.
key_points: COMA uses action-corruption to steer correct vulnerability diagnoses to flawed remediations and verdict-flips to destabilize exploitability verdicts via reachability chains.
Action-corruption successfully compromised all five tested models, including frontier reasoning models, across synthetic domains and real-world CVE-2021-33813.
Attacks succeed specifically when the disambiguating fact must be inferred by the model rather than directly read from the retrieved documents.
CCD uses leave-one-out causal influence measurement to flag answers relying on low-trust documents, identifying attacker-controlled documents without false positives on tested benign controls.
summary.why_it_matters: Security-RAG systems can be reliably manipulated using entirely true, non-contradictory retrieved documents, necessitating causal auditing defenses like CCD.

security.title: The Model's Tell: Measuring Context-Leakage Attack Signals with Behavior Gauges

summary.tldr: LeakGauge detects context-leakage attacks in LLMs by appending a content-agnostic behavior-gauging suffix and computing an attack-risk score from its prefill token probabilities.
key_points: Appends a content-agnostic suffix verbalizing leakage behavior to gauge model responses before decoding.
Achieves an AUROC range of 0.944 to 0.996 across 11 LLMs, including GLM-5.2 (753B) and Kimi-K3 (2.8T), on unseen attacks.
Demonstrates signal stability across language changes and shifts from verbatim to semantic disclosure.
Enables an input detector with under 0.5K additional parameters and an added latency of 10.34 ms.
Validates via activation-steering interventions that the risk score correlates with internal leakage-related representation directions.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a lightweight, highly accurate method to detect context-leakage risks without needing internal hidden-state extraction or access to LLM activations during deployment.

security.title: MobileWorldSafety: Benchmarking GUI Agent Safety Against Environmental Injection Attacks in Android Apps

summary.tldr: MobileWorldSafety is a new benchmark featuring 142 real-world Android risk tasks to evaluate LLM-powered mobile GUI agents against environmental injection attacks.
key_points: Evaluates agent safety against indirect prompt injections and adversarial instructions across standard Android app environments.
Utilizes a two-stage evaluation pipeline combining rule-based verification of system states with an LLM judge for ambiguous cases to isolate safety failures from capability failures.
Benchmark results across six general and specialized GUI agents reveal attack success rates between 40.4% and 66.9%.
summary.why_it_matters: Current mobile GUI agents consistently fail safety alignment when encountering untrusted contextual content, highlighting an urgent need for security measures before real-world deployment.

security.title: HarnessRisk: A Lifecycle-Oriented Benchmark for Agent Harness Safety

summary.tldr: HarnessRisk is a lifecycle-oriented benchmark evaluating LLM agent harness safety across six operational phases using 128 sandboxed test cases.
key_points: Evaluates safety across six phases: Harness Configuration, Capability Extension, Runtime Operation, State Persistence, Action Control, and Incident Recovery.
Benchmarked 14 model and harness configurations across three harnesses and six LLMs, revealing attack success rates between 12.6% and 80.9% alongside high utility (75.0% to 97.6%).
Identified Harness Configuration as the most vulnerable phase, where attacks succeed by modifying security-sensitive parameters in authorized workflows.
Discovered that explicit risk recognition fails to prevent execution, with some configurations detecting risks in over 90% of runs while still suffering substantial attack success.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that agent safety cannot rely solely on model-level risk detection and requires evaluating security across the entire operational lifecycle of the harness.

security.title: Reflex-Guard: A Low-Latency Guardrail for LLM Prompt Safety Using Dense Semantic Embeddings

summary.tldr: Reflex-Guard is a local LLM guardrail that achieves 95.9% harmful prompt recall at 37.6 ms end-to-end latency using jailbreak-aware preprocessing, sentence-transformer embeddings, and seven binary classifiers.
key_points: Reduces prompt safety filtering latency to 37.6 ms, outperforming baseline models like Llama Guard 2 (255 ms) and SafeDecoding (723 ms).
Uses jailbreak-aware preprocessing, compact sentence-transformer embeddings, and seven fast binary classifiers to process prompts locally.
Achieves 100% detection on GCG suffix attacks and Base64-encoded prompts at default thresholds, while structured DrAttack prompts require a lowered threshold of 0.03.
Demonstrates a Reflex Efficiency Score (RES) of up to 16.79 on a evaluation dataset of 30,568 samples across five sources.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables sub-100 ms real-time safety filtering for LLM applications locally, avoiding the high latencies and privacy risks of external moderation APIs.

security.title: KeyPooling: Measuring Where LLM API Relay Paths Collapse Prompt Cache Isolation

summary.tldr: KeyPooling is a measurement method that identifies where LLM API relays collapse prompt cache isolation, revealing that shared upstream credentials enable cross-account cache reads across major open-source gateways and commercial services like OpenRouter.
key_points: Tested five open-source gateways using OpenAI and Anthropic, finding none bound individual customers to upstream credentials by default, exposing cross-customer cache reads under shared credentials.
Audited OpenRouter's weekly frame (covering 80.5% of eligible token volume) and found cross-account cache reads occurred in 12 of 28 provider labels, representing 33.7% of volume.
Demonstrated side-channel risks by recovering eight consecutive target positions on a production route without direct access to the target.

Proposed a defense contract requiring provider-enforced customer domains or authenticated namespaces, which preserves most prompt reuse at a 1.7–2.5% cost increase when placed after shared public prefixes.
summary.why_it_matters: LLM API aggregators and gateways that multiplex requests onto shared upstream credentials inadvertently destroy prompt cache isolation, enabling cross-tenant side-channel attacks and data leakage.

security.title: Fair ASR: Re-Evaluating Black-Box Jailbreaks under Shared Target-Call Budgets

summary.tldr: Fair-ASR introduces a target-call budget protocol for black-box LLM jailbreaks, exposing budget-dependent ranking shifts and enabling ReCode, a compositional attack achieving 85% ASR on GPT-5 within 20 target calls.
key_points: Fair-ASR establishes a standardized evaluation protocol using target-model calls as a uniform comparison axis, while tracking attacker calls independently to measure operational efficiency.

Re-evaluating 11 black-box attacks demonstrated that attack success rankings fluctuate significantly across target-call budgets, with simple stochastic perturbations and hand-crafted templates outperforming complex LLM-driven methods under equal access.

ReCode combines desensitization rewriting with two low-cost primitives identified via Fair-ASR, achieving an 85% ASR on GPT-5 using a 20 target-call budget and an average of 7.19 attacker calls per request.
summary.why_it_matters: Standardizing jailbreak benchmarking around explicit query budgets prevents misleading safety claims and guides the development of compute-efficient red-teaming methods.

security.title: When Agents Act on Web3: An Attack-Surface Survey of MCP, Skills, and Tool Calling

summary.tldr: This survey introduces an attack-surface taxonomy and risk-mapping matrix for Web3 AI agents, showing existing defenses stop under 30% of attacks while model-level safety refuses fewer than 3%.
key_points: State-modifying actions in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem have increased from 27% to 65% of tool use.

Four blockchain properties—irreversibility, signing authority, continuous autonomy, and sequence-level composition—qualitatively alter threat models by converting recoverable software failures into irreversible losses.
The authors map MCP, skills, and tool-calling attack classes against execution-layer amplifiers, representative mitigations, and residual security gaps.
Empirical evaluation shows measured protections mitigate fewer than 30% of attacks, and model-level safety mechanisms refuse under 3%.
summary.why_it_matters: Current agent safety frameworks and model-level refusals fail to prevent the vast majority of exploits when AI agents manage execution authority on public blockchains.

security.title: COMIC: Reference-Aware Safety Gating for Multimodal Large Language Models

summary.tldr: COMIC introduces a reference-aware pre-generation safety gate that evaluates explicit operation-target pairs to defend MLLMs against localized multimodal jailbreaks.
key_points: Identifies a safety failure mode where harmless prompts and images become unsafe only when an operation (e.g., summarizing, translating) is bound to a specific visual target.
Combines OCR and open-vocabulary proposals to construct candidate targets and grounds plausible referents before generation.
Evaluates safety over explicit operation-target pairs rather than moderating the prompt-image pair as a single holistic input.
Applies max-risk aggregation with quality-aware routing to conservatively handle ambiguous visual targets and decide whether to block or forward requests.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents MLLM jailbreaks that exploit visual reference resolution without degrading model utility on benign, reference-sensitive inputs.

security.title: PACE: Policy-Attested Contract Execution for Safe AI Agents in Decentralized Finance

summary.tldr: PACE introduces a transaction-level authorization framework that uses signed Policy Decision Records to cryptographically bind LLM agent transaction intents to deterministic on-chain smart account execution.
key_points: Uses typed transaction intents, a deterministic verifier, and signed Policy Decision Records (PDRs) to bind intent, policy, and simulation reports to exact execution bytes with replay and expiration protection.
Implements an on-chain Solidity smart account that enforces PDR signatures with a measured gas overhead of 29,826 to 31,822 gas.
Achieved a 0.00 unsafe execution rate and 0.00 false-positive rate across 2,800 trials on 40 tasks in a deterministic sandbox, compared to an 0.80 unsafe rate for unguarded baselines.
Ablation analysis showed that permissive policy settings (+57.5 pp) and touched-contract allowlists (+12.5 pp) are the primary drivers of execution safety.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents malicious or hallucinated LLM outputs from executing unauthorized DeFi transactions by enforcing cryptographic, deterministic policy verification before on-chain execution.

security.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models

summary.tldr: "Fool's Gold" is a defensive deception method for open-weight models that yields confident, falsified decoy responses to hazardous requests after safety alignment is stripped via abliteration attacks.
key_points: Trains decoys inside a differentiable simulation of abliteration attacks, using a refusal pin and benign leash to preserve original clean-state capabilities.
Evaluated on seven dense and MoE models (9B–122B); six passed efficacy gates, yielding decoy responses on 0.51–0.90 of attacked-state requests with no detectable clean-state degradation.

Falsified answers are observationally indistinguishable from correct ones without independent ground truth, driving error rates on a 122B model's CBRNE-adjacent benchmark slice to 0.82–0.86 (vs. <= 0.10 undefended).
Repeated sampling (K=64 element-wise consensus) reduces usable procedure reconstruction to 0.083–0.625 (vs. 0.58–0.96 undefended), leaving users with no label-free method to verify correctness.
Applies exclusively to initial open-weight releases against post-release safety-removal attacks, and does not mitigate in-context jailbreaks.
summary.why_it_matters: It renders abliterated open-weight models unreliable for malicious operational requests by poisoning the outputs with indistinguishable, falsified details rather than attempting to prevent weight modification.

security.title: Authorization Before Context: A Model-Neutral Audience Boundary Against Cross-Audience Memory Leakage in Agentic Systems

summary.tldr: A model-neutral invariant called "authorization before context" prevents cross-audience memory leakage in agentic systems by filtering memory items against current channel viewers before context assembly.
key_points: Applies an anti-monotone audience-membership rule at the memory-to-context transition, admitting memory items only if all current viewers belonged to the item's original recording audience.
Reads the current viewer set from channel metadata, falling back to public when metadata is ambiguous or inconsistent.
Enforces security by exclusion prior to model invocation, rendering the boundary model-neutral and resilient against poisoned memories attempting to widen their audience.

Evaluated on a synthetic Contextual-Integrity suite where the boundary completely eliminated forbidden facts from assembled contexts compared to unscoped baselines, failing closed on all audited read paths.
summary.why_it_matters: It deterministically guarantees data privacy in agentic memory retrieval by removing unauthorized context before LLM processing, eliminating reliance on non-deterministic model compliance.

summary.tldr: Two papers show frontier LLMs frequently violate contextual integrity by inappropriately leaking persistent memory attributes, but training models to explicitly reason about CI using RL significantly reduces leakage without sacrificing utility.
key_points: Evaluations using the CIMemories benchmark revealed frontier models exhibit up to 69% attribute-level information leaks, with GPT-5 violations escalating from 0.1% to 25.1% across repeated runs and multiple tasks.
Privacy-conscious prompting fails to fix CI violations, causing LLMs to overgeneralize by either withholding all data or leaking everything.

Explicitly prompting LLMs to reason about contextual integrity, combined with an RL framework trained on 700 synthetic examples, substantially decreased unauthorized disclosures while preserving task performance.
The reasoning and RL approach successfully transferred performance improvements to human-annotated CI benchmarks like PrivacyLens.
summary.why_it_matters: As autonomous AI agents rely on persistent user memory, scaling and basic prompting are insufficient to prevent privacy leaks, requiring specialized reasoning and RL training frameworks to enforce context-dependent data protection.
